transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I just can’t seem to get a full night’s sleep anymore, my mind won’t let me rest and I wake up feeling exhausted. It has gotten to the point where I'm just too tired to function properly during the day.
How long has this sleep problem been going on, and do you have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early?

This has been going on for about a year now, starting around the time my mother's health began to decline. I struggle with both; I lie awake until 1 or 2 in the morning with my mind racing about my mom and my work, and even when I do drift off, I keep waking up every couple of hours. It leaves me feeling completely unrefreshed by the morning.
Do you usually have enough time and opportunity to sleep, or are there nights when you simply cannot sleep even though your schedule would allow it?

Yes, I absolutely have the time and opportunity to sleep, but my mind simply won't let me. I go to bed around 11 PM intending to rest, but I end up lying awake until 1 or 2 in the morning because my brain is constantly racing with worries about my mom and my work responsibilities.
Besides the sleep problem, do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things most days, such as work, family, finances, or your health, and feeling unable to control the worry?

Yes, my mind is constantly scanning for what could go wrong, whether it's my mother's health, a server crash at work, or even just a missed bill. I try to tell myself to stop, but the worries just keep looping and multiplying, constantly interrupting my attempts to focus on my Bible study or crochet.
When you’re worrying, do you also get physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, feeling on edge, fatigue, trouble concentrating, or irritability?

Yes, I feel wound tight all the time, constantly pacing or tapping my foot like I'm bracing for an emergency, and I've been snapping at my husband and brother over tiny things. I also feel constantly drained, and my concentration is so poor that I find myself rereading the same reports at work because I just can't focus.

Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, dizziness, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?

No, I don't experience those sudden, overwhelming panic attacks or things like a racing heart or dizziness. For me, it's more of a constant, daily state of tension and worry that just never seems to let up.
Do you ever have unwanted, intrusive thoughts that you feel driven to neutralize with repeated behaviors or rituals, like checking, counting, or washing?

No, I don't have any rituals or repetitive behaviors like washing, counting, or checking. My mind definitely loops through worries and contingency plans constantly, but I don't perform any physical actions to try to stop them.
Over the past year, have you also been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I have pulled back from things I normally love, like my Saturday walking club, crocheting, and church activities. It is not that I feel deeply hopeless, but I am just too physically exhausted from the lack of sleep to participate. My mind is also so distracted by constant worries and feeling on edge that I can't seem to focus on or enjoy them anymore.
Do you feel unable to sleep even when you are relaxed and have enough time to rest, or is the main problem that worries keep your mind active and prevent you from falling asleep?

The main problem is definitely my mind racing with worries, as I rarely feel relaxed lately because my body is always wound so tight. As soon as I lie down, my brain immediately starts running through backup plans for work or worrying about my mother's health, making it impossible to drift off.

When you have trouble sleeping, is it mainly because your mind is racing with worries and tension, or do you also have nights when you simply cannot sleep even when you feel calm and not particularly worried?

It is almost always because my mind is racing with worries and my body feels so tense. I lie awake running through backup plans for work or imagining worst-case scenarios about my mother. I honestly can't remember the last time I felt calm enough at night to even see if I could sleep without those worries.

When you have trouble sleeping, is it mainly because your mind is racing with worries and tension, or do you also have nights when you simply cannot sleep even when you feel calm and not particularly worried?

It really is entirely because of the worries and tension; I don't have nights where I feel calm but still can't sleep. I lie awake for hours with my mind running through backup plans for work or worrying about my mother falling. Even when I do finally drift off, I keep jolting awake every couple of hours because my body is so tense.
Have these worries and tension been present more days than not for at least 6 months, and have they made it hard to work, manage home life, or enjoy your usual activities?

Yes, this constant worry and tension has been going on almost every day for about a year now, ever since my mother's health crises began. It has definitely impacted my life, making it hard to focus at work where I constantly have to reread network reports, and causing me to pull back from my church activities and walking group because I'm just too drained and distracted to participate.
Over the past year, have you also had a persistently low mood, or felt hopeless or worthless most days?
No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or worthless at all. It is more that I feel extremely exhausted, overwhelmed, and constantly anxious or worried about everything going on around me.
Do you have trouble sleeping even on nights when you feel calm and not particularly worried, or is the sleep problem only when your mind is racing with anxiety and tension?

I rarely have nights where I feel truly calm anymore because I feel wound tight all the time. My sleep issues are almost always accompanied by my mind racing with worries about my mother's health or work contingencies, making it impossible to rest.
Do you have trouble sleeping only because of the worries and tension, or do you also have nights when you feel calm and still cannot fall asleep?

It is strictly due to the worries and tension, as I rarely feel truly calm these days. My body is always far too wound up to relax, and my mind is constantly running through "what if" scenarios about my mother or my work. I never have nights where I feel calm and still can't sleep, because the anxiety is always present.
